  • Critical pathway is defined as management plan to describe about the schedule or timing of the actions that are to be done to achieve the goal on time. It includes placement of the tasks according to their priority.
  • Grading is to describe and represent about the level of achievement by a student or an employee. A person is graded depending upon his performance as A, B and so on. It may be used to grade educational institutions and companies on the basis of their quality and performance.
  • Supervision is to supervise or observe someone’s activity, performance or ability to do any work such as supervising a student’s clinical procedure in hospital by his/her teacher, supervision of employees while they have been assigned with a task.

  • Amebiasis is amebic dysentery and is usually treated with anti-parasite medications, such as nitroimidazole drugs to kill amoeba in the blood. Commonly used nitroimidazole drugs are metronidazole, tinidazole.
  • For bacterial infections, antibiotics are effective. Some common drugs are amoxicillin, augmentin (Potassium clavulanate), ciprofloxacin, etc.
  • Antimicrobial drugs are used to kill microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi and protozoans. It may be antibiotics, antiseptics and disinfectants.

choices.title: Dysphagia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Dysphagia is the term used for difficulty in swallowing. Dysphagia can occur as a result of any throat infections such as sore throat, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, etc. Other causes may be tumor in neck, swelling, enlarged thyroid, etc.
  • Dysphoria is the state of uneasiness or unhappiness or dissatisfaction. It may result due to any mental illness specifically in depression, anxiety or agitation.
  • Regurgitation is the backflow or the action of bringing swallowed food up again to the mouth. It may be associated with any disease such as gastroesophageal reflux disease, pyloric stenosis or Zenker’s diverticulum, i.e. formation of an abnormal pouch in esophagus.
  • Dyspnea is called difficulty in breathing or shortness of breath. It can result due to any underlying conditions such as asthma, COPD, pneumonia, anxiety situations, etc.

It’s a 10 cm horizontal or vertical unruled line. This scale is much easier to use by the patient to express his/her level of pain.
  • Graphic rating scale is generally a performance appraisal method, which demonstrates person’s traits and behavior which are important for effective performance in the organization. It may be presented as four or five parameters starting with unsatisfactory performance to excellent performance of an individual and he is rated according to his performance.
  • Semantic differential scale is a rating scale which measures the attitude of the respondent toward any given object and he chooses appropriate position on a scale having two adjectives, e.g. warm or cold, strong or weak, etc.
  • A checklist is a tool used in various organizational settings to keep an appropriate list of items, objects or procedures. In a hospital setting, a checklist is used to identify and note the steps of procedure done or not, list of items required for surgery, etc.

choices.title: Regression
choices.correct_explanation:
• An ego defense mechanism when an adult throwing a temper tantrum when he does not get his own way is called regression. This is also known as movement back in psychological time when one is faced with stress.
  • Repression is a defense mechanism in which disturbing and threatening thoughts or feelings are kept out of becoming conscious. For example, a person has childhood memories of being abused may later have difficulty in forming relationships.
  • Undoing is a defense mechanism in which person tries to remove unhealthy thought by engaging in contrary behavior. For example, if a person being violent with someone, he tries to become overly wise to him.

choices.title: Yellow bag
choices.correct_explanation:

  • Blue bag includes waste related to glassware and is discarded in cardboard boxes with blue-colored marking.
  • Red bag includes contaminated recyclable waste such as tubing, bottles, intravenous tubes, sets, catheters, urine bags, syringes without needles and gloves.

choices.title: Hypoxia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Cardiac output alters or increases as a result of hypoxia. It is most common in high altitudes due to release of adrenaline. Other causes such as fever due to increased oxidative process, anemia and hyperthyroidism as a result of increased metabolism lead to an increase in cardiac output.
  • Cardiac output decreases in all other three conditions, i.e. in congestive heart failure, it results due to weak muscle contractility.
  • In arrhythmias, cardiac output decreases due to incomplete filling of the left ventricle due to rapid activity of the heart.
  • In shock condition, due to poor circulation and lack of pumping action of the heart, cardiac output decreases eventually.

choices.title: Cells
choices.correct_explanation:
• The cell is the basic structural, functional and biological unit of living organisms. This is the smallest unit of life. Cells are also known as building blocks of life.
  • Enzymes are called catalysts which accelerate chemical reactions. They speed up the rate of chemical reactions that occur within the cells. They help in digestion and metabolism.
  • Proton is a sub-atomic particle with a positive electric charge and a mass slightly less than that of a neutron.
  • A neutron is a sub-atomic particle of about same mass as proton but without an electric charge, present in all atomic nuclei except in ordinary hydrogen.

choices.correct_explanation:

  • Placenta battledore is characterized by presence or attachment of umbilical cord to the margin of the placenta.
  • Placenta velamentous means the cord separates into small vessels instead of entering placenta directly. This occurs mainly due to multiple gestations.
  • Placenta previa is a condition in which the placenta is situated low in the uterus or is called low-lying placenta. It is characterized by painless vaginal bleeding leading to the abortion of the fetus.

choices.title: Down syndrome
choices.correct_explanation:
• Down's syndrome is known as trisomy 21, caused due to presence of third copy of chromosome 21. It is characterized by physical growth delays, decreased muscle tone, short neck, flat face, small head, low set ears and mouth, single palmer crease, etc.
  • Turner's syndrome is featured by presence of only one X chromosome in female or can be called 45X or 45X0. The main characteristics are short stature, non-functioning ovaries, puffiness and swelling (lymphedema) of neck called webbed neck, heart defects, skeletal abnormalities, etc.
  • Edward Syndrome is known as trisomy 18, resulting due to presence of a third copy of chromosome 18. Most common characteristics are low birthweight, small and abnormally shaped head, small jaw and mouth, long fingers that may overlap, low set ears, left lip and palate, etc.
  • Klinefelter syndrome is known to have two or more X chromosomes in males, i.e. 47 XXY. The main features are small, firm testes, small penis, sparse pubic, armpit and facial hair, gynecomastia, tall stature, etc.

choices.title: Confidentiality
choices.correct_explanation:
• Confidentiality means keeping patient’s personal and medial information private and assuring him/her about privacy of data regarding disease, diagnosis and treatment as well as other personal information.
  • Accountability refers to a fact or condition for which one is answerable or accountable. For example, a nurse must be accountable for any task or procedure done on the patient.
  • Unity refers to be united or work as a team such as nursing or health team  work together to achieve quality of care by reducing time and increasing work force in inpatient care.
  • Flexibility in medical terms refers to the ability to be easily modified in situations where being rigid is not beneficial or worthy. One can be flexible in situations when we need to get the work done by the team as a leader.

choices.title: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone
choices.correct_explanation:
• Melanocyte-stimulating hormone is responsible for the formation of linea nigra in pregnancy, which appears on the abdomen. Melanocyte-stimulating hormone is made by the placenta.
  • Progesterone is a hormone that is secreted by female reproductive system. It regulates and maintains the integrity of inner lining of the endometrium of the uterus. It is produced by the ovaries, placenta and adrenal glands.
  • Human placental lactogen is released by the placenta during pregnancy. Human placental lactogen level rises as the fetus grows. It also acts as antagonist for insulin, i.e. anti-insulin properties.
  • Human chorionic gonadotropin is a hormone which is produced by the placenta after implantation supporting the ovarian corpus luteum. It supports the endometrial lining for maintaining the pregnancy.

choices.title: Anorexia nervosa
choices.correct_explanation:
• Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in which patient has a fear of becoming obese and eats less or induces vomiting to become thin. Patient with anorexia nervosa is so lean and suffers from fluid and electrolyte imbalance.
  • Bulimia nervosa is characterized by excessive eating or “binge eating”. The patient eats more and also induces vomiting when over-eating is done to avoid weight gain.
  • Pica is also an eating disorder characterized by patients eating non-eatable items, such as diet, paint chips, chalk pieces, hair, etc.
  • Dieting is a practice of eating the food in a balanced manner including essential nutrients. Dieting helps to reduce weight and addresses the problems related to obesity.

questions.title: Psychological eating disorder in which there is an intense fear of becoming obese is called:

choices.title: Milia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Milia are tiny distended sebaceous glands which appear as white dots on nose and face of newborn. These may also occur at any age. They disappear within a few weeks or months.
  • Erythema is known as redness of skin or mucous membrane, which is caused by hyperemia in capillaries located superficially. Erythema can occur as a result of any injury, infection or inflammation.
  • Stork bite is a birth mark in the newborn and it is temporary. This is also called nevus simplex. It is caused by dilation of tiny blood vessels or capillaries in newborn and is visible beneath the skin.
  • Mongolian spots are the birth mark caused by pigment in the skin. It is present at birth and it appears in the infant’s first week of life.

choices.title: Glomerulonephritis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hypertension occurs as a result of glomerulonephritis in children due to damage to kidney function. Glomerulonephritis leads to damage in tubules of the kidney resulting in loss of functioning and causes increased blood pressure. Kidney is responsible for maintained blood pressure by maintained renin angiotensin mechanism. In case of glomerulonephritis, the alteration in kidney function will have the scarcity of renin angiotensin mechanism. So, it causes hypertension.
  • Arrhythmia usually occurs as a result of hypertension but is not responsible to cause hypertension. Arrhythmia will not cause hypertension whereas hypertension may cause cardiac arrhythmias.
  • Dehydration also causes hypertension as if the cells lack water, so the brain sends signal to pituitary gland to secrete vasopressin which leads to constriction of blood vessels and eventually hypertension.
  • Hypothyroidism is a cause of secondary hypertension. It results due to increased peripheral vascular resistance. So, the most common cause in children is glomerulonephritis.

  • Subjective data are the information described by the patient and are called ‘symptoms’ i.e. patient’s feeling, concerns regarding health states, etc.

  • Convenience sampling is a method of nonprobability sampling techniques. Here, the researcher selects the participants according to convenience or ease to get sample. People are selected on the basis of their availability.
  • Cluster sampling is done by dividing the population into separate groups or clusters when it is difficult to know the whole population.

choices.title: Menopause
choices.correct_explanation:
• Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation or when menstrual periods are no longer there and female cannot get pregnant. There is a natural decline in the reproductive hormones when a woman reaches 40s or 50s.
  • Menarche is the occurrence of first menstruation or first menstruation cycle. The normal average age of menarche varies between 12 and 13 years of age.
  • Amenorrhea is the absence of menstruation during the reproductive years.
  • Pregnancy is a condition or period of being pregnant. Medically, pregnancy is defined as period from conception to birth. After the egg is fertilized by a sperm and then is implanted in the lining of the uterus, it develops into the placenta and embryo and becomes a fetus.

choices.title: Epidermis
choices.correct_explanation:
• A superficial layer of the skin is called epidermis and it is composed of stratified keratinized squamous epithelium. There are no blood vessels and nerve endings in the epidermis.
  • Dermis is the thick layer present below the epidermis which forms the true skin. It contains blood vessels, capillaries, nerve endings, sweat glands, hair follicles as well as other structures.
  • Sebaceous glands have the secretory epithelial cells and they secrete oily antimicrobial substance, i.e. sebum. It is present all over the body parts except palms of the hands and soles of the feet.
  • Hair grow from the hair follicles, and they are the down growth of epidermal cells into the dermis or subcutaneous tissue.

choices.title: Community
choices.correct_explanation:
• Community is defined as a group of people living in the same place or having a particular characteristic in common.

  • A pre-experimental research design is a design in which the researcher deals with only experimental group. This design lacks a control group. It may be a one group pre-test, post-test study.
  • A descriptive research design is referred to a design in which one has to decrease the characteristics of a population or phenomena, which is being studied.
  • Non-experimental research design is used when the research does not seem to be feasible and it is not possible to manipulate the independent variable. This design mainly assesses the knowledge, attitude, beliefs and behavior of people.

choices.title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
choices.correct_explanation:
• Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is a lifesaving procedure used in emergency in patients with cardiopulmonary arrest to promote oxygenated blood flow to the heart and the brain.
  • Permanent pacemaker is a self-contained device which is implanted in a pocket beneath the patient’s skin. It is indicated for patients with myocardial infarction, persistent bradyarrhythmia, complete heart block, etc.
  • Cardioversion is a procedure to send electric shocks to the heart by placing electrodes on chest and abnormally fast heart rate or cardiac arrhythmia is converted to a normal rhythm.
  • Temporary pacemaker is an external battery-powered pulse generator and a lead or electrode system. It is used in emergency and may be transcutaneous, transvenous, transthoracic and epicardial type. Among them transcutaneous is best choice.

questions.title: What is the emergency treatment of cardiopulmonary arrest?

choices.title: Myringotomy
choices.correct_explanation:
• Myringotomy is a procedure in which an incision is made in tympanic membrane for the treatment of acute otitis media (AOM). It is mainly done to relieve pressure in the ear and to drain fluid from the ear in infection.
  • Mastoidectomy is the removal of mastoid cells which are diseased or infected. It may be simple radical mastoidectomy. Simple mastoidectomy involves removal of mastoid cortex and exenterating the mastoid air cells. Radical involves the removal of mastoid bridge.
  • Stapedectomy is a surgical procedure in which the extra bone formed outside the stapes, which prevents the stapes to move normally, is removed to improve hearing. The most common indication is otosclerosis.
  • Tympanoplasty is a procedure of reconstruction of the ear drum or small bones of ear (Ossicles). It is done in case of perforation due to any infection of middle ear.

questions.title: What is the intervention for acute serous Otitis media?

choices.title: Dysmenorrhea
choices.correct_explanation:
• Dysmenorrhea is a term used to describe pain during menstruation or it can be called painful menstruation. It may be primary or secondary. Secondary occurs due to any underlying disease condition such as endometriosis.
  • Dysuria is a term used for painful urination or discomfort during urination. It occurs as a result of any infection of urinary tract. Sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are also the cause behind dysuria.
  • Dysphagia is referred to as difficulty in swallowing. It occurs as a result of any disease or in sore throat, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, etc.
  • Dystocia is a term used for abnormal labor. Labor may be abnormal in various circumstances such as obstructed labor, precipitated labor, large size of baby, pelvic structure abnormalities.

questions.title: Medical term for pain associated with menstruation is called ____________.

choices.title: Hearing aids
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hearing aids are the mechanical device used by patients with hearing problem or who have difficulty in hearing. It improves hearing by making the sound audible to a person who has hearing loss.
  • Lip reading or speech reading is a method or technique of understanding speech by interpreting the movement of lips, face and tongue. It is also useful for deaf persons.
  • Speech therapy is a therapy to improve a child’s speech ability and to understand or express the language. This can be performed by speech therapist and language pathologist.
  • Sign language is also a technique used for deaf persons so that they can make use of visual movements in understanding the speech or language.

choices.title: Passive immunization
choices.correct_explanation:
• Human serum given after dog bite to prevent rabies is a type of passive immunization. Passive immunity is a process of providing IgG antibodies to protect against any infection.
  • Active immunization refers to immunity in which antibodies develop in person’s immune system after exposure of body to any antigen through disease, e.g. flu, chickenpox, etc.
  • Immunomodulation is a process in which the immune response is altered to a desired level. It may be natural or human induced such as homeostasis is natural and immunotherapy from outside is human-induced modulation.
  • Toxoid is an inactivated toxin whose toxicity is suppressed by chemical or heat treatment. Most commonly used toxoid is tetanus toxoid.

choices.title: Nursing process
choices.correct_explanation:
• Nursing process is considered based on concept framework as it defines the conceptualization and articulation of concepts, facts, propositions and theories, and focused patient care.
  • Patient’s feedback is the positive or negative response given by the patient in regard to the medical or nursing care received by the patient.
  • Nursing process is based on same phenomena from identifying patient’s problem to organization of issues and solving the problem depending on need of the patient to achieve a goal.
  • Other options are not an example of conceptual framework. Patient’s feedback is the response about care given to patient. Progress notes are the details of patient toward stage of recovery and days of patient care. Progressive patient care means continuous patient care including comprehensive need-based treatment.

choices.title: Grand mal seizures
choices.correct_explanation:
• Grand mal seizures are generalized seizures and most common generalized seizure is tonic-clonic. It includes three phases as an aura, a tonic-clonic seizure and postictal lethargy.
  • Petit mal seizures are known as absence seizures. It leads to temporary loss of awareness resulting in lack of continuity in learning environment.
  • Atonic seizures are called deep seizures or akinetic seizures that involve partial or complete loss of muscle tone which occurs as a result of transient alteration in brain functioning.
  • Bilateral seizures start from a focal seizure which starts in one area of the brain and spreads to both sides of the brain leading to tonic-clonic seizure. It lasts usually 1-3 minutes but takes long time to recover.

questions.title: Generalized tonic clonic seizures in childhood are called:

choices.title: Hemiplegia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hemiplegia means either side of the body, i.e. paralysis of an arm and leg on same side of the body. It occurs due to upper motor neuron lesion. Most common causes are meningitis, encephalitis, degenerative disorders, stroke, cerebral palsy, etc.
  • Paraplegia involves paralysis of lower extremities. The most common reason is injury to the spinal cord.
  • Quadriplegia presents paralysis of all four extremities. It can also be called tetraplegia.
  • Monoplegia is paralysis occurring in one limb or in a particular region of body. It occurs usually in single limb, commonly in arm.

questions.title: A condition where one side of the body is paralyzed is called___________.

choices.title: Colostrum
choices.correct_explanation:
• Colostrum is the first form of milk secreted by breast during first 3 days following delivery. It is thin, watery and yellow fluid which consists of proteins, sugar, fat, water, minerals, vitamins and maternal antibodies. It is easy to digest and provides adequate nutrition for newborn.
  • Foremilk is the milk flowing from alveolar cells, forms constantly and flows through small tubules to reservoirs of milk.
  • Hind milk is secreted toward the end of breastfeeding and it contains more fat and energy.
  • Transitional milk is secreted following colostrum. It is secreted during first 2 weeks of postnatal period. This milk contains high fat and sugar and low protein and immunoglobulin content.

questions.title: First form of milk secreted by breast during the first three days following delivery is called __________.

choices.title: Debridement
choices.correct_explanation:
• Debridement is a process of surgical removal of infected or dead tissue from the wound. It is done to promote healing and can be performed surgically, chemically or by autolytic removal of the tissues.
  • Dehiscence is a term used for a wound postoperatively where a wound gets ruptured along a surgical incision.
  • Incision is an intentional surgical cut made during any surgical procedure or operations. Incision can be a small or a large cut made under aseptic conditions.
  • Drainage is to release pus or pressure which builds up under the skin due to an abscess, soiled or infected paranasal sinus.
  • Debulking is a reduction of bulk of a tumor. This is called cytoreduction or cytoreductive surgery.

questions.title: Surgical removal of infected or dead tissue from the wound is called _________.

choices.title: Olfactory nerve
choices.correct_explanation:
• Olfactory nerve is cranial nerve I, which helps in the function of smell and is a sensory type of nerve. Its function is assessed by asking client to close eyes and identify different aromas, such as coffee, orange, etc.
  • Optic nerve is cranial nerve II, which has a role in vision and visual fields. Its function can be assessed for the client’s vision and reading by Snellen chart, checking visual fields by confrontation and conducting an ophthalmic examination.
  • Oculomotor nerve is cranial nerve III, which is a motor nerve and helps in the extraocular eye movements and movement of sphincter of pupil as well as ciliary muscles of lens. The function can be assessed by assessing six ocular movements and pupil reaction.
  • Trochlear nerve is cranial nerve IV which is a motor nerve and its function is extraocular eye movements, especially, movement of eyeballs downward and laterally. It can be understood by assessing six ocular movements.

choices.title: 1.010–1.025
choices.correct_explanation:

It may occur in conditions such as dehydration, hepatic disorders and nephrosis. Low specific gravity is present in conditions, such as failure to reabsorb water that concentrates urine and indicates hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, alkalosis, acute renal failure and diabetes insipidus. Specific gravity is measured with a urinometer with a specially calibrated hydrometer which floats in cylinder of urine. The higher it floats, the greater will be specific gravity.
  • Options “a”, ”b” and “d” are denoting the higher specific gravity of urine.

choices.title: Human chorionic gonadotropin
choices.correct_explanation:

  • Human chorionic somatomammotropin (HCS) is another name for human placental lactogen (HPL) which is a polypeptide placental hormone.
  • Human papilloma virus is a viral sexually transmitted infection spread through skin-to-skin contact.
  • Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is a gene complex, which encodes the major histocompatibility complex proteins in humans. These proteins are responsible for regulations of immune system in humans.

questions.title: In choriocarcinoma, which hormone’s level is high?

choices.title: Uterine prolapse
choices.correct_explanation:
• Uterine prolapse is a condition where the uterus descends into the vagina or comes out. It could result due to weak pelvic floor muscles or during delivery of placenta when force is applied. The women can feel that something is coming out of vagina. There is feeling as if the person sitting on a small ball.
  • Cord prolapse is a condition when the cord is felt as the presenting part on vaginal examination. Cord prolapse is a complication and can lead to cord compression and eventually fetal anoxia.
  • Disc prolapse is condition where the outer fibers of intervertebral disc are injured and the nucleus pulposus, i.e. a soft material from its enclosed space ruptures out of spinal bones.
  • Rectal prolapse occurs when the rectum loses its attachment and telescopes out through the anus. It could result due to multiple births, vaginal delivery, etc. due to force exerted on the part of the intestine.

questions.title: ____________ is the condition in women which gives them a feeling of something coming out from vagina.

choices.title: Demography
choices.correct_explanation:
• Demography is the study of the human population, its size, structure and distribution. It can also be defined as study of statistics, i.e. birth, death, income and incidence of disease, which describes the dynamic structure of population of human.
  • A survey is a method to obtain or gather information about people or individuals or any research to collect data from study participants. A survey focuses on collection of facts, etc.
  • Ecology is a branch of biology that deals with relations of organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings including both biotic and abiotic components.
  • Epidemiology is the study of distribution and determinants of health and disease condition in a defined population. It also covers possible control of diseases and other factors relating to health.

questions.title: The statistical study of human population, its size, structure and distribution is called ___________.

choices.title: Anticoagulants
choices.correct_explanation:
• The use of Anticoagulants is to prevent blood clot. Therefore, if the patient is on mechanical valves, he requires lifelong anticoagulants as they prevent formation of clots over the mechanical valves in the heart.
  • Antipyretics are the medications used to lower the body temperature in fever and the examples are: aspirin, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, etc.
  • Analgesics are used to relieve pain. They act on peripheral and central nervous system. Common examples are codeine, hydrocodone, morphine, etc.
  • Antibiotics are the drugs used to treat bacterial infections. Most commonly used is Amoxicillin or potassium clavulanate (Augmentin) to treat bacterial infections.

questions.title: People with mechanical valves require to take these medications lifelong:

choices.title: Lifestyle factors
choices.correct_explanation:
• Lifestyle factors include the factors which can be modified to attain a healthy body and good physique, such as activity or exercise, good nutrition, family planning, stress reduction, no violence, etc.
  • Physical factors include the factors, like genetic inheritance, disability, sensory impairments, age, gender, etc.
  • Mental factors include one’s self esteem, confidence, family, decision making, concentration, self-worth, etc.
  • Social factors include culture, community, family, organization, society, religion, language, etc.

questions.title: Physical activity, good nutrition, family planning, reduced stress, absence of violence are:

choices.title: Vestibulocochlear
choices.correct_explanation:
• Vestibulocochlear nerve or auditory nerve is cranial nerve VIII which has the function to maintain balance and helps in hearing. It originates from the cochlea, i.e. inner ear.
  • Vagus nerve is Xth cranial nerve which is the longest of all cranial nerves and controls the inner nerve center, i.e. parasympathetic nervous system and is also called pneumogastric nerve.
  • Facial nerve or cranial nerve VII, which controls the muscles of facial expression and functions to convey taste sensations from anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
  • Trochlear is cranial nerve IV and a motor nerve controlling the movement of superior oblique muscle of the eyes. This is the smallest of the cranial nerves having longest intracranial course.

questions.title: This nerve maintains hearing and balance:

choices.title: Implied
choices.correct_explanation:
• An implied consent is taken when in an emergency situation, the patient is unable to give consent or an informed consent and there is no immediate family member is available to make decision. Implied consent is the consent which is not been expressly granted by the person, but rather implicitly granted by the individual’s actions, facts and circumstances in a particular situation.
  • There is no such term, ‘Absent consent’ in healthcare.
  • A written informed consent is that the patient has full understanding of the risks and the benefits of the treatment which is going to be done on him such as any surgery or procedures.
  • Process consent is an ongoing consensual process involving mutual decision making between a nurse and a patient where a patient is informed about all the stages of the treatment process.

questions.title: A type of consent in case of medical emergency, where doctors start emergency treatment to patients who cannot give informed consent, and for whom no immediate family member is available to make such decisions:

choices.title: Clean wound
choices.correct_explanation:
• Wound that is made by a surgeon making a surgical incision as under aseptic conditions is considered to be a clean wound. As it is followed by aseptic technique, therefore, it is free from any contamination.
  • A puncture wound occurs as a result of any sharp injury or penetration of any pointed object such as nail, splinter, nail file, or a knife. Puncture wounds are easily infected.
  • A contusion is a type of hematoma or a bruise or a region of injured tissue or skin with a rupture of blood capillaries.
  • Infected wound occurs when pathogenic organisms invade into viable tissues surrounding the wound. A wound becomes infected due to inappropriate care such as septic environment or not following aseptic precautions while wound care.

questions.title: Wound made by surgical incision, by a surgeon under aseptic condition is called _____________.

choices.title: Kernicterus
choices.correct_explanation:
• Kernicterus is a condition characterized by abnormal accumulation of bilirubin in the brain causing brain damage or metabolic encephalopathy. It occurs due to accumulation of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and untreated jaundice in newborn.
  • Isoimmunization is defined as development of antibodies against the antigens of another individual of the same species. It is also called Rh sensitization.
  • Jaundice is represented by yellow discoloration of the skin, mucous membranes and sclera of the eyes which is caused due to high bilirubin levels in the blood.
  • Cephalohematoma is a condition presented as subperiosteal hematoma which occurs under the skin in periosteum of the skull bone of a newborn or an infant.

questions.title: Brain damage caused by accumulation of abnormal levels of toxic bilirubin in the brain is known as ___________.

choices.title: Gastrostomy tube
choices.correct_explanation:
• Feeding tube which is placed directly into the stomach by making an artificial opening in the abdominal wall is called gastrostomy tube. It is mainly done in patients with dysphagia, malnutrition, esophageal cancer, etc.
  • A nasogastric tube is placed from nose to the stomach and is also known as Ryles tube or an NG tube.
  • A nasoduodenal tube is placed through the nose into the duodenum. The common indication for placing this tube when there is any gastric irritation such as ulcers and patient requires immediate nutrition.
  • Jejunostomy is the procedure in which a soft J-shaped tube is placed through the skin of abdomen into the jejunum of small intestine. Some specific indications are protein energy malnutrition, comatose or depressed sensorium, liver failure or critical illness.

questions.title: A feeding tube placed directly into the stomach through the artificial opening on the abdominal wall is called __________.

choices.title: Nursing assessment
choices.correct_explanation:
• Nursing assessment is a process of collecting, analyzing, documenting the client data and identifying the needs of the patient. Assessment is done by the history, conducting physical assessment and reviewing client’s records.
  • Nursing diagnosis is a process of analyzing and synthesizing the collected data and can be done by comparisons, identifying gaps and formulating appropriate diagnosis for patient.
  • Intervention is a phase in which the nurse makes priority to solve client’s problems and find out the ways to solve the issue related to the client.
  • Evaluation is the measurement of the goals and outcomes to know that they are achieved or not. The nurse seeks outcome and improvement in patient’s condition after implementation of the interventions.

questions.title: Systematic collection of patient’s data to identify unmet human needs:

choices.title: Closed group
choices.correct_explanation:
• In closed groups, all members join at the same time and only those members can participate in all the sessions.
  • In an open group, new members could join the group any time. So, there is no fixed group strength.
  • Homogeneous group means a group with similar diagnostic backgrounds, for example, all persons were survivors of earthquake victims, those who had depression, etc.
  • Heterogeneous group means those having mixed members with different issues and have different emotional problems.

questions.title: Psychotherapy groups in which all members of the group, join the group at the same time and have a defined membership is called __________.

choices.title: Ventilator
choices.correct_explanation:
• Ventilator or Mechanical ventilator is an artificial-assisted device, which provides or assists in spontaneous breathing to those who are unable to do efforts of breathing.
  • Defibrillator is a device which delivers electric current or shock to the heart to get its electrical activity or get back the rhythm and conduction. It is used in case of ventricular fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia.
  • Pacemaker is an artificial device that is placed in the chest or abdomen for maintaining heart rhythms. This is mainly used to treat arrhythmias.
  • Spirometer is a device used to measure the volume of air, i.e. inspired or expired by the lungs and checks the movement of air in and out of the lungs. Patients who are at low risk need flow incentive spirometer and those at high-risk need a volume incentive spirometer.

questions.title: An individual who is unable to breathe, needs the support of the ________.

choices.title: Esteem need
choices.correct_explanation:
• According to Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, the human need to get value and respect from others is called self-esteem need, i.e. feeling of independence and esteem from others.

Figure: Maslow’s hierarchy of needs

·        Stimulation need is the form of motivation factor in order to achieve the goal.

questions.title: The human need to get value and respect from others is called:

choices.title: Myelography
choices.correct_explanation:
• Myelography is a procedure of visualization of spinal cord by introducing a spinal needle into spinal canal and injecting a contrast material in the spinal cord.
  • Echoencephalography is a method by which abnormalities within the cranial cavity can be detected. It can be performed by using high frequency sound pulses which are delivered through a probe held firmly to the scalp.
  • Electromyography (EMG) is used to assess the health status of muscles and nerve cells which control the motor neurons. Electromyography (EMG) helps to explore muscle dysfunction, nerve dysfunction, or issues with the nerve-to-muscle signals transmission.
  • Electroencephalography, i.e. EEG measures the electrical activity of the brain. It is done by placing electrodes over scalp and usually noninvasive.

questions.title: X-ray examination of the spinal cord and vertebral canal following introduction of contrast media into the spinal subarachnoid space is called __________.

choices.title: Microteaching
choices.correct_explanation:
• Microteaching is a social skill teaching to provide feedback to teacher trainee for modification of teacher behavior. This method can be applied or used in a small group consisting of 5-10 pupil and the duration of microteaching is 5-10 minutes.
  • Lecture method is the method which is mainly teacher-controlled and can be used in classrooms to teach students.
  • Role play is a method to teach in a way that students explore realistic situations such as by acting and developing interpersonal skills of the learners. They can participate and perform the role of character they are reading.
  • Symposium is a conference or a meeting in which speakers are present to speak on particular topics to solve common problem. Symposium is usually completed in a single day, whereas conference may have pre-conference discussions and it could continue for a couple of days.

questions.title: Which among the following is a teacher training and faculty development technique where the teacher teaches 5-10 pupil for 5-10 minutes:

choices.title: Patent ductus arteriosus
choices.correct_explanation:
• Patent ductus arteriosus is a condition characterized by persistent opening or connection between pulmonary artery and aorta. Normally, the opening, i.e. ductus arteriosus closes shortly after birth. But if it fails to close after birth, it can lead to abnormal flow of blood from aorta to pulmonary artery.
  • Transposition of great vessels means the aorta arises from the right ventricle whereas pulmonary artery arises from the left ventricle which is abnormal.
  • Atrial septal defect is a congenital birth defect causing hole in the wall between the right and left atrium of the heart.
  • Ventricular septal defect is also a congenital birth defect presenting hole in the wall of the lower chambers of the heart, i.e. right and left ventricle and the blood passes from left to right side of the heart.

questions.title: Which among the following is a medical condition in which there is the connection between pulmonary artery and aorta?

choices.title: Precocious puberty
choices.correct_explanation:
• Onset of puberty before age of 8 years in girls is called precocious puberty.
  • Thelarche denotes the secondary breast development.
  • Menarche is defined as the onset of first menstruation in females or first cycle of menstruation. The usual age of menarche ranges between 9-15 years of age with an average of 13 years.
  • Delayed puberty is when there is absence of beginning of sexual maturation or incomplete development of sexual characteristics.

questions.title: Onset of puberty before the age of 8 years in girls is called ____________.

choices.title: Hirschsprung disease
choices.correct_explanation:
• Failure to pass meconium within first 36 hours of life, abdominal distension, poor feeding and empty rectum are all features of Hirschsprung's disease or aganglionic megacolon. It can lead to constipation in newborns due to absence of ganglion cells preventing motility in intestine.
  • Appendicitis is defined as inflammation of the appendix.
  • Malabsorption is a term used to describe lack of absorption of nutrients through the small intestine.
  • Peritonitis is defined as inflammation of the peritoneum or the membrane which lines the abdominal wall that covers the abdominal organs.

questions.title: Failure to pass meconium within first 36 hours of life, abdominal distension, poor feeding and empty rectum are the findings of:

choices.title: Ectopic pregnancy
choices.correct_explanation:
• When the conceptus implants outside the uterine cavity, it is called ectopic pregnancy. There may be various abnormal sites of implantation such as the most common site is fallopian tubes and parts can be ampulla (70%), isthmus (12%), fimbriae (11%) and cornea (02%).
  • Molar pregnancy is an abnormal form of pregnancy characterized by development of non-cancerous tumor which forms in the uterus due to a nonviable fertilized egg in the uterus.
  • Antepartum hemorrhage is defined as bleeding from or into the genital tract after 28th week of pregnancy but before the birth of the baby. The main causes of antepartum placental bleeding are placenta previa, abruptio placenta, extra placental causes such as cervical polyp, carcinoma of cervix, etc.
  • Abortion is defined as ending of pregnancy done by expulsion of embryo before it is viable.

questions.title: Abnormal pregnancy in which the conceptus implants outside the uterine cavity is called:

choices.title: Mean
choices.correct_explanation: • Mean is the average and the most common method to derive the central tendency. It is the average of all the values for a variable. Median and mode are also the measures of central tendency but do not measure the average. Median is the value that falls in the middle of the distributed numbers. Mode is the value that occurs frequently in a given set of distributed numbers. Standard deviation, range and inter-quartile range are all measures of dispersion. So, mean is the correct answer.

questions.title: Average that is used to derive the central tendency:

choices.title: Thrombosis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Formation of clots in veins is called thrombosis. It is static and if it gets dislodged from the vein, it can travel as an embolus in the circulation and can lead to further complication such as pulmonary embolism and stroke.
  • Aneurysm is defined as weakening of the wall of arteries where an artery can easily bulge out due to weakened vessels. It can occur due to hypertension, atherosclerosis or any trauma.
  • Atherosclerosis is a term for building up of plaques in the arteries. It can be caused due to deposition of cholesterol, fat, calcium, etc. which can lead to narrowing of arteries.
  • Ischemia is defined as lack of blood in the heart muscles to myocardial ischemia and inadequate blood supply to the muscles of the heart preventing the muscle to get enough oxygen.

questions.title: Development of clots in the vein is called ____________.

choices.title: Parkinson disease
choices.correct_explanation:
• Mask-like facial expressions are the features of Parkinson’s disease. There are five stages of Parkinson’s disease, which start with an initial stage of unilateral limb involvement, hand and arm trembling and progress to second stage, i.e. mild stage and characterized by bilateral limb involvement and mask-like face with slow and shuffling gait. Stage 3 involves postural instability, leading to stage 4 characterized by bradykinesia, akinesia, rigidity and at last complete ADL dependence in stage 5. Mask-like face or hypomimia occurs in Parkinson’s disease because the nerve supplies to the 43 muscles in the face get affected.
  • Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder in which the primary symptom is ptosis, i.e. drooping of eyelids.
  • Alzheimer’s disease is an irreversible and progressive brain disorder which is characterized by memory loss and disturbed thinking skills.
  • Huntington’s chorea is an inherited disorder caused due to break down of nerve cells in the brain and the first sign which appears in this condition is uncontrolled movement of arms, legs, head face and the upper body.

Figure : Shuffling gait in Parkinson’s disease

questions.title: A neurological disorder in which the patient will have expressions of mask-like face and staring is known as ______________.

choices.title: Hepatitis B
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hepatitis B is known as serum hepatitis. It is an infection caused by HBV (Hepatitis B Virus). It affects the liver leading to failure or cancer of liver which can be fatal too. Hepatitis B virus spreads through blood, semen or other body fluids infected with Hepatitis B. Hence, Hepatitis B is called  serum Hepatitis
  • Hepatitis E is a liver disease caused due to Hepatitis E virus. The mode of transmission is through fecal-oral route.
  • Hepatitis A is also a liver disease caused due to Hepatitis A virus. Mode of transmission is similar to Hepatitis E and incubation period is 15-45 days.
  • Bacterial hepatitis or infection of liver mainly occurs due to Gram negative enteric or pneumococci. Bacterial infection can cause abscess in liver, acute hepatitis, hepatic tuberculosis, peritonitis, empyema and related serious complications.
